steps.title: Two runs of one workload
steps.text: The widget runs one workload twice: under the legacy collector on the left, and under PEP 848's incremental collector on the right. Both runs allocate the same objects in the same order, and the allocation clock along the bottom of each panel counts the MB allocated so far.

marks.note: The legacy run's heap: its whole line on top, then a lane for each of its spaces.
The incremental run's. Its top line runs with the legacy one, since both runs hold the same objects.

steps.title: Reference counting frees most objects
steps.text: CPython frees an object as soon as the last reference to it goes. json_loads models a worker that parses JSON 60 times a loop and drops each result as the call returns.

marks.note: The heap levels off below 1.2 MB, while the run allocates 21 MB.

steps.title: Cycles stay behind
steps.text: Two objects that refer to each other keep each other alive after the program drops them: cyclic garbage, which only a cycle collector frees. Here a tenth of the worker's churn starts a cycle.

marks.note: The pale band is uncollected garbage. It widens to 1.0 MB by 12 MB, then holds between 1.0 and 1.2 MB, as young collections free cycles as fast as the churn makes them.

steps.title: A collection frees them
steps.text: A collection takes a group of objects and frees those no reference from outside the group reaches. The legacy collector's gen 0 collection takes the objects allocated since the last one, every threshold0 kB, here 1,000.

marks.note: Freed, in red, sits in every bar: the cycles that came loose since the collection before.

steps.title: Most work keeps objects
steps.text: Each object a collection examines and keeps is work that frees nothing. Early in the run the worker builds the objects it keeps to the end, and each collection examines them.

marks.note: From 1 to 5 MB, survived, in violet, outweighs freed two or three to one.
Yield, the share of examined objects a collection frees: 45.9% for the legacy collector, 70.5% for the incremental.

steps.title: Older objects, fewer looks
steps.text: PEP 848 spends the collector's work on older objects, likelier to be cyclic garbage. Its incremental collector lets an object age 10 to 12 MB here before it examines it, and examines it once. It takes the old generation an increment at a time, between young collections.

marks.note: Its first bar comes at 11 MB. The bars at 19 and 21 MB free cycles and keep nothing.
284 work per MB for the legacy collector, 228 for the incremental.

steps.title: Three generations
steps.text: The legacy collector splits the heap into three generations: the nursery, where new objects start, the aging generation and the old generation. connected_components' module loads a graph of 1.4 million dicts and keeps it to the end.

marks.note: The old lane fills in stairs, as gen 1 collections move the graph in.

steps.title: Gen 0 and gen 1
steps.text: Every threshold0 kB, here 1,000, the collector runs a collection. Most are gen 0 collections, which take the nursery. Once more than threshold1 of them, 10, have run since the last gen 1, the next is a gen 1 collection, which takes the nursery and the aging generation together and moves what survives into the old generation.

marks.note: As the graph loads, each gen 0 collection examines 806 or 807 objects: refcounting has freed the rest of the 1,000 kB, read_adjlist's churn. Each gen 1 collection, every 12 MB, examines about 9,700 from the third on.

steps.title: Gen 2 takes the whole heap
steps.text: A gen 2 collection comes once more than threshold2 gen 1 collections, 10, have run since the last gen 2: here at the 133rd collection, 133 MB into the run. It examines the whole heap in one go.

marks.note: The tall bar at 133 MB holds the gen 2 collection, examining the whole graph.
91.4K objects in that one collection, against the incremental collector's 10.2K.

steps.title: A quarter holds gen 2 back
steps.text: Lower threshold2 to 2, and gen 2 collections come every 37 collections while the graph loads. After the first, a gen 2 collection also waits until gen 1 collections have moved in a quarter of what the last gen 2 left in the old generation.

marks.note: Gen 2 collections at 37, 74 and 111 MB, each larger than the last. None comes at 148 or 185 MB: the graph has stopped growing.
3 gen 2 collections.

steps.title: The incremental collector, for contrast
steps.text: The incremental collector takes the old generation an increment at a time. read_adjlist's frame holds the graph while it loads, so sys reaches none of it. One old collection, at 40 MB, takes _adj, the dict that holds each node's adjacency dict, with most of the young adjacency dicts and edges.

marks.note: Its tallest bar, at 40 MB, holds 10.2K objects, against the legacy collector's 91.4K.

steps.title: New objects wait
steps.text: The incremental collector holds new objects in its young generation: the nursery, then threshold1 / 2 aging spaces. A young collection examines the oldest aging space and moves what survives into the old generation. At a threshold0 of 1,000 kB, the young generation holds 12 MB.

marks.note: The worker's objects sit in the nursery and aging lanes. Visited stays empty until the young collection at 11 MB, the first to reach the worker's objects.

steps.title: Every object is work
steps.text: json_loads models a worker that calls json.loads 60 times a loop. No result holds a cycle, so each object a collection examines is work that frees nothing.

marks.note: Survived, in violet, fills each bar: the collection examined objects still in use.
The same violet. Freed, in red, stays a sliver until shutdown.

steps.title: The legacy collector looks twice
steps.text: A gen 0 collection examines the nursery every threshold0 kB, here 1,000. At 12 MB, a gen 1 collection examines the survivors again before they reach the old generation.

marks.note: From 1 to 5 MB, gen 0 collections examine the objects the worker builds. The tall bar at 12 MB is the gen 1 collection examining all 1,145 again.

steps.title: The incremental collector looks once
steps.text: The incremental collector first examines an object when its aging space is the oldest: 10 to 12 MB after its allocation at this threshold0.

marks.note: At 11, 13, 15 and 17 MB, young collections move the worker's objects from the aging lane into visited, an aging space at a time.
Four bars, at 11, 13, 15 and 17 MB, examine each object once.

steps.title: Work per MB adds it up
steps.text: Work per MB divides each collector's work, shutdown's included, by the 21 MB the run allocates.

marks.note: 192 against 136: the legacy collector examined the worker's objects twice.

steps.title: The PEP's threshold0
steps.text: At the PEP's threshold0 of 2,000 kB, the young generation holds 24 MB and the 21 MB run ends first. The incremental collector examines nothing before shutdown.

marks.note: No bar before shutdown.
Both fall. The incremental collector's 82 is shutdown's work alone, and the legacy collector's run ends before its first gen 1.

steps.title: Gen 2 fits the run
steps.text: Lower threshold0 to 120 kB, and gen 1 collections come often enough for a gen 2 collection to fit. It examines the worker's objects a third time: 249 work per MB against 136.

marks.note: Gen 1 bars every 1.44 MB while the worker builds its objects, and the gen 2 collection's tall bar at 16 MB.
One gen 2 collection for the legacy collector. The incremental collector runs no sweep.

steps.title: A longer aging generation
steps.text: Raise threshold1 to 20, and the aging generation holds 10 aging spaces. The young generation grows to 22 MB, past the run. Only what the worker allocated in its first MB ages through it, and one young collection, at 21 MB, examines those 266 objects.

marks.note: The aging lane holds most of the worker's objects to the end. Visited takes 258 at 21 MB.
One bar before shutdown, at 21 MB.

steps.title: Pending and visited
steps.text: The incremental collector splits the old generation into two spaces, pending and visited. Young collections move their survivors into visited. async_tree_io_tg builds a tree of asyncio tasks four times over, 55.4 MB at most, and drops each once its tasks finish.

marks.note: The old generation's lane fills as young collections move a tree in, and empties as the tree goes.

steps.title: A sweep
steps.text: Each old collection, between two young ones, moves objects from pending to visited. Once pending runs empty, the two swap: visited, holding the whole old generation, becomes the new pending, and a new sweep starts.

marks.note: 12 sweeps: the first five end at 44, 100, 160, 192 and 228 MB. In every other one, young objects carry pending's tag, so marking chases the young tasks each tree adds.

steps.title: Marking first
steps.text: An old collection first marks: it moves the pending objects sys reaches to visited without examining them, since nothing sys reaches is garbage. sys reaches the task tree through the event loop, so the old collections mark it.

marks.note: Marked, in olive, fills about half of each bar: each old collection marks what the young collection before it moved in, about 1,900 objects.

steps.title: The budget paces it
steps.text: The work budget sets how much each old collection takes. Each young collection adds its survivors, and the old collection after it marks or examines until it has spent the budget.

marks.note: From 44 MB on, each young collection lifts the budget, to 1,933 while a tree grows, and the old collection after it spends it back to zero.

steps.title: The legacy collector beside it
steps.text: The legacy collector's gen 1 collections take the nursery and the aging generation together, and its one gen 2 collection takes the whole heap.

marks.note: The tallest bars hold gen 1 collections, up to 13,576 objects each. The gen 2 collection, at 266 MB, comes between two trees and examines 1,763.
891 against 577. As each run ends, the legacy collector's gen 0 collections examine what the finishing tasks allocate.

steps.title: A smaller tree
steps.text: Shrink the task tree to 100 kB, the slider's smallest. Young collections move too little into the old generation to lift the budget above zero.

marks.note: No sweep runs.

steps.title: The largest tree
steps.text: Grow the task tree to 62,200 kB, the slider's largest. The legacy collector's gen 2 collection comes while a tree lives, and examines it with the rest of the heap.

marks.note: The gen 2 collection's bar at 266 MB stands more than three times as tall as the tallest gen 1 bar.
50.9K for that gen 2 collection, against 1.9K for the incremental collector.

steps.title: Where the budget starts
steps.text: The work budget, work_to_do in the PEP's pseudocode and old_work on the reference branch, starts at -100,000 real objects: -6,250 simulated ones, each standing for 16. Old collections wait while it stays below zero.

marks.note: The line holds at -6,250 until 22 MB, while each young collection takes an aging space still empty.

steps.title: Young collections pay it back
steps.text: Each young collection adds what it moved into the old generation to the budget.

marks.note: The young collections from 22 to 42 MB, every 4 MB, lift it above zero. At 44 MB the first old collection finds pending empty and swaps the spaces, which ends the first sweep, then marks until it has spent the budget.
12 sweeps over the run.

steps.title: Credit for what an increment frees
steps.text: An old collection debits the budget with each object it marks or examines. Once it ends, it credits the budget with twice each object its increments freed, so the old collections after one that finds much cyclic garbage take more, and the sweep ends sooner. The multiplier here is 10, five times the PEP's.

marks.note: Still 12: the old collections here free nothing, so the credit adds nothing.

steps.title: A lower start
steps.text: Start the budget at -200,000 real objects, twice the PEP's.

marks.note: The line starts at -12,500, and the first old collection waits until 56 MB.
12 sweeps.

steps.title: A start at zero
steps.text: Start the budget at 0. The young generation's 24 MB holds the first old collection back instead.

marks.note: The first sweep ends at 24 MB.
13 sweeps.

steps.title: A start above zero
steps.text: Start the budget at 50,000. The first old collection, at 4 MB, finds the old generation empty and swaps the spaces. Young objects now carry pending's tag, so it marks sys and the 900 young objects sys reaches, finds the old generation empty again, swaps the spaces back and sets the budget to zero.

marks.note: 15 sweeps, two of them at 4 MB, against 13 for a start at 0.

steps.title: Trees that turn into garbage
steps.text: Swap the task tree for a tree whose objects keep their links back to their parents, and each tree turns into cyclic garbage as it goes. Now the old collections free whole trees, and the credit counts.

marks.note: Increments at 172, 444 and 484 MB free three of the four trees, 55,429 objects each.
10 sweeps.

steps.title: No credit
steps.text: Set the multiplier to 0, and an increment that frees a tree pays nothing back into the budget.

marks.note: Increments at 172, 324 and 500 MB free three trees.
6 sweeps, against 10.

steps.title: Where cyclic garbage waits
steps.text: The incremental collector first examines a new object once it has aged through the young generation, 24 MB at the PEP's defaults. The legacy collector's gen 0 collections take the nursery every threshold0 kB, 2,000 here. json_loads' run ends after 21 MB.

marks.note: 0.8 MB in both columns: start-up's two trees, which turn into cyclic garbage at shutdown.

steps.title: A tenth of the churn makes cycles
steps.text: Let a tenth of the worker's churn start cycles. The incremental collector examines no young object before the run ends, so each cycle waits for shutdown.

marks.note: The band of uncollected garbage widens through the run.
1.9 MB against the legacy collector's 0.8.
174 for the incremental collector against 229: it does less work, and leaves the garbage.

steps.title: Half the churn
steps.text: Let half the churn start cycles, the slider's most. Half of what the loops allocate waits for shutdown.

marks.note: 10.1 MB against 1.0.

steps.title: A smaller young generation
steps.text: Lower threshold0 to 1,000 kB, with a tenth of the churn starting cycles. The young generation shrinks to 12 MB, and the run outlasts it.

marks.note: 1.2 MB for the incremental collector, once its young collections free cycles.
228 against 284: its young collections now examine the loops' objects.

steps.title: A large program
steps.text: The PEP expects peak memory to come out about the same, and bounds the extra a small program pays at 24 MB. A large program can come out ahead: here async_tree_io_tg, with a tenth of its churn starting cycles that live 10 MB on average.

marks.note: 5.5 MB for the legacy collector, which leaves old cycles to its next gen 2 collection, against 1.2.
1,534 against 734.

steps.title: An increment is a closure
steps.text: An increment is pending's last object and every object it reaches that carries pending's tag. An old collection examines it whole, however little of the work budget is left. In every other sweep young objects carry pending's tag too. connected_components' module loads its graph inside read_adjlist, whose frame holds it until the call returns, so sys reaches none of the graph while it loads.

marks.note: Two bars stand out. At 48 MB an old collection takes _node's increment: _node, the dict that holds each node's attribute dict, and those attribute dicts, 5.3K objects in all. At 60 MB it takes _adj's: _adj, the adjacency dicts it holds and their edges, 14.3K objects, 12.1K of them young.

steps.title: Peak work
steps.text: The collection at 60 MB is the incremental collector's peak work. _adj's increment takes three quarters of the young generation, 12 MB of the graph's load.

marks.note: 14.3K, the collection at 60 MB, below the legacy collector's 19.4K, a gen 1 collection.

steps.title: The budget pays for it
steps.text: The collection at 60 MB cost 14.3K objects against a budget of 2,439, and old collections wait while the budget stays below zero. Each young collection credits the budget with the survivors it moves in. The next six find the aging spaces _adj's increment emptied and move in 427 to 1,960 objects each. At 96 MB an old collection takes pending's last 13 objects, read_adjlist's reader among them, and ends the sweep.

marks.note: At 60 MB the line drops to -11,844. It climbs back until the young collection at 94 MB lifts it above zero.

steps.title: Half the graph
steps.text: Halve the graph, to 45,000 kB. It still loads at 48 and 60 MB, so the increments there take as much as before.

marks.note: 14.3K, as with the whole graph.

steps.title: A quarter of the graph
steps.text: Shrink the graph to 22,000 kB. It has loaded by 42 MB, and _adj's increment at 56 MB takes what of it is still pending or young.

marks.note: 7.4K, half the whole graph's 14.3K.

steps.title: A program's own collections
steps.text: gc.collect() with no argument takes the whole heap under either collector. Each of create_gc_cycles' loops calls it, builds 100 rings of 21 real objects, drops them and calls it again.

marks.note: The band of ticks under the top lane marks the calls, one tick a pixel at most.

steps.title: No room for the runtime's own
steps.text: Each collection resets the countdown to the next one the runtime starts. The calls come closer together than threshold0 kB, so once the loops begin, the runtime starts none.

marks.note: 1,029 in each column: the runtime's 2, at 2 and 4 MB, then 1,024 calls and shutdown's 3.

steps.title: The same work either way
steps.text: A program that calls gc.collect() this often does the same work under either collector, give or take 0.1%.

marks.note: Faded bars, full collections, of the same height in both columns.
12.7K against 12.6K.

steps.title: Yield differs
steps.text: The incremental collector marks what sys reaches without examining it, and yield divides what a collection frees by what it examined.

marks.note: 22.2% against 5.5%: about a fifth of what the incremental collector examines is rings it frees.

steps.title: Peak work leaves the calls out
steps.text: Peak work counts the collections the runtime started, and leaves the calls out.

marks.note: 531 for the legacy collector's gen 0 collection at 2 MB, and 0 for the incremental collector, whose young generation the run never fills.

steps.title: Shutdown
steps.text: Shutdown runs three full collections. The first frees nothing, since the last loop's call freed its rings. Once the modules go, the second frees the tree with parent pointers, cyclic garbage once sys lets go of it. The third finds nothing left.

marks.note: At 98 MB, past the dashed line, the heap falls from 1.1 MB to nothing.

steps.title: Below a loop's build
steps.text: Lower threshold0 to 100 kB, below the 132 kB a loop's rings take to build. The runtime's own collections come back, inside each build.

marks.note: Gen 0 collections examine rings the loop is building. Over the whole run they free 13 objects, start-up's.
Young collections examine 972 objects over the whole run: each gc.collect() takes the whole young generation with it.

steps.title: What the thresholds mean
steps.text: The PEP keeps gc.set_threshold() and its three numbers, and changes what they mean. threshold0 is the size of a half-space in kB: the nursery is two, and a collection comes each time the program allocates threshold0 kB. threshold1 counts the aging generation's half-spaces. The young generation comes to threshold0 × (threshold1 + 2) kB, 24 MB at the defaults.

marks.note: 102 in each column: one every 2 MB of the 199 MB run, and shutdown's 3. The reference branch counts threshold0 in kB for the legacy collector too.

steps.title: Halve threshold0
steps.text: Halve threshold0 to 1,000 kB. The incremental collector's collections double, and each takes half as much.

marks.note: 201 in each column, against 102 at 2,000 kB.
Young collections examine at most 1,613 objects each, against 3,226 at 2,000 kB.

steps.title: Peak work parts ways
steps.text: The incremental collector's peak work falls too: its largest collection is the one that takes _adj's increment, and at 1,000 kB it comes sooner, at 40 MB, while less of the graph has loaded. The legacy collector's leaps.

marks.note: The incremental collector's falls from 14.3K to 10.2K. The legacy collector's leaps from 19.4K to 91.4K: a gen 2 collection, at 133 MB, takes the whole graph.

steps.title: Raise threshold1
steps.text: Raise threshold1 to 20, and the young generation grows to 44 MB. The graph outlasts it either way, but reaches the old generation later, and the old collections start later.

marks.note: The first old collection to mark more than a few objects comes at 64 MB, against 44.

steps.title: threshold1 for the legacy collector
steps.text: Lower threshold1 to 2. The legacy collector's gen 1 collections come every fourth collection, and two gen 2 collections fit the run.

marks.note: Gen 2 collections at 90 and 180 MB examine the whole heap: 63.3K objects as the graph loads, then 91.4K once it has.
2 gen 2 collections.
